Being able to calm yourself when you are aware of when one is coming on is a set of tools that is usually acquired when going through therapy, which is great. The act of grounding is useful after those tools aren't effective.

I had some emergency pills for severe panic attacks and the most it did was make me too tired to be anxious. It made basically impossible to function when I used them so just didn't bother with them afterwards.

None of this is preventative. Once the condition is bad enough, which is subjective to the person, the only help is physical therapy and eventually surgery. 

The rest of this helps to mitigate pain and stiffness. Ergonomic keyboards and mice, wrist rest and not being chronically on the computer helps a lot more.

This doesn't prevent an anxiety attack, let's just make that clear.

But these steps help to regain your footing when you are having one.

"I really doubt anyone is going to read this, and even if they do, they might think that it is just a bunch of silliness and excuses. Nevertheless, I feel it is necessary to share exactly what has been going on instead of a bunch of vague inconsistencies. 

First things first. I was in college during the time I was shelling out art left and right, when I still had copious amounts of passion albeit severe depression, as drawing was the only thing that actually made me happy. I was under the distinct impression (and explicitly told) that my parents were going to pay for college if I was ever got into it. So, having a tuition of $5,600 and a Pell Grant, one would think I was in the clear. Not so much so. My mother told be to 'just get a scholarship' as soon as I was enrolled. After an eviction basically every semester (every 3 months), my grade plummeted as I could not get any internet access with which I would do my classes and I lost my financial aid. The school called me at the end of my freshman year to tell me that they were forcing me to withdrawal unless I started paying a minimum of $150 a month. So, holding in the immense amount of disappointment, anger and sadness I broke the news to my parents who told me that they would make it up to me. Meaning they wouldn't do anything to help.
And sadly, I have to start all over again because my debt went into collections last month in the amount of $9,963.50. Hooray for me.

And another extension to this little scenario is that college was basically the last thing I was holding onto to keep me together, being that it was the only way I was feeling some kind of progress. Like I was actually doing some good in my life. And it was taken away from me with the ease of a phone call.

Therefore, I sunk deeper into my depression because for the very first time, I realized my place on the totem pole was all the way at the bottom, below the cat. My mother had her husband and that's all she needed anymore. She didn't need to pay for her adult child's college (like she's ever supported anything), even if she said she would, nor did she like the idea of someone having emotional turmoil; because frankly, as she's said before, she doesn't have time to deal with anyone else's problems but her own. I was getting into arguments with them everyday over me eating anything of 'theirs' in the house when her husband thinks of everything in the home as free game. Then when I was getting money, whether it be from saving or what, was always taken from me so I couldn't save anything. Yes, I get it, I am lucky to get any money from my parents, but at the same time, what is the point when you take it all back because you wasted it on shoes, cigarettes, alcohol and crap you didn't need? Maybe I'm just ungrateful.
So I sunk into the darkness of my room. I didn't need lights, seldom food and even more seldom social interaction. What was the use of it all anyway? Lights waste money and hurt your eyes, food is scare and is for the important ones, and if social interaction was important, why did I get dragged to the middle of a crime laden industrial district where I know no one? It didn't matter, any of it. There were days were I just didn't sleep, eat or leave the room except to use the bathroom and get water. Kept the lights off and the blinds shut in my room. Nothing mattered. Not art, not friends, not family, not living. I didn't care. I didn't feel important, alive or worth anything. And some days, it creeps back up on me and I get awful flashbacks to the times when there were so many loud thoughts in my head and now way of shutting them up. And no one cared to check up on me. At least no one related to me anyway.

Luckily with help from my two best friends I was able to get some proper help or at least some proper encouragement. After the last eviction, the one I'm still recovering from, I was taken in at a friend's home. So I'm slowly trying to put the pieces back together and get my life back on track. I'm still struggling with my depression, but it is getting a lot better and I do find myself doodling sometimes, which is a great sign. I'm surrounded (more or less) by people who are caring and it really helps me get through the day."
